observation.visible_scene: A wooden floor holds several parallel domino runs, each a line of blue-based dominoes topped with a single color. From top to bottom: a loose flat scatter of green dominoes, a long orange-topped run, a red-topped run, a green-topped run, and an orange-topped run at the bottom, with blue-topped curve connectors at the left and right ends linking the runs into serpentine paths. The camera is fixed; the wood grain does not shift.
visible_changes: At the start the upper orange run is already mostly toppled in its middle and right; only a few upright orange pieces remain at its far left, and these fall flat within the first ~6 frames, after which the orange run is static.

The red run's left end begins tilting around frame 9-10 and a falling front travels steadily left-to-right along the red run for the rest of the clip (front near the middle by frame 25, near the right curve by frame 35-40).

The lower green run stays fully upright until about frame 36-37, when its right end (fed by the red run's right curve) starts toppling; the green fall then begins propagating right-to-left, with only the rightmost few green pieces down by the last frame.
The bottom orange run and the top scattered green pile show no change throughout; the long blue line at upper left is static.
outside_clip_unknowns: What initiated the red run's fall before frame 1, and whether the orange run's earlier collapse was part of the same chain.
Whether the green run's right-to-left topple continues to completion, and whether it would then trigger the bottom orange run.
The cause of the already-flat orange and green piles at the very start.
uncertain_details: Exact physical connection between the red run's right curve and the green run's right end is inferred from the serpentine layout, not directly confirmed as a contact event.
The bottom orange run may begin falling just after the clip ends; its state is unchanged within the excerpt.
